business: REPAIHUB: online service that moves money from an Indian NRO account to a Canadian bank account, with the Indian tax forms and CA certificate handled
by_segment: Newer immigrant (PR < 5 yrs) with modest NRO balance (under ₹5L)
Property seller / inheritor with a lump sum (₹20L-₹1Cr waiting in NRO)
Retiree / parent-age with Indian pension or rental income (₹3L-₹15L a year)
Settled mid-career professional with old FDs, rent or savings in NRO (₹5L-₹20L)
why_not: I have never heard of REPAIHUB and I only move money through my own bank's NRI desk. My NRO balance is small, so I would not risk it with a new company over a few hundred dollars of savings.
I have never heard of them and nobody in our WhatsApp group or temple association has used them. I do not move money on a stranger's advertisement, however nice the guarantee sounds.
My cousin in India already handles this kind of thing for me and doesn't charge a rupee. Paying $199 to a company I've never heard of, when I have a person I trust, doesn't make sense to me.

The money has sat in NRO for years and I keep saying I'll sort it on the next trip. It sounds sensible, but I wouldn't actually get around to it this month, and I'd want to check it with my accountant first.

My relative in India can sort this out for free, and I compare everything to the paisa. Paying CAD $149-199 on top of the bank's rate to move a sum my family could help me with does not add up for me.

why_yes: My lump sum from the property is big enough that I don't want to gamble it on a cousin's informal swap. A named RBI-authorised bank, a FINTRAC number and fee-only-on-arrival is what I'd want, and the fee is small next to the amount.

Fee only on arrival plus the refund guarantee takes most of the risk off me, and the free CA call is what I'd want anyway. At about 1.25% to skip the forms and an India trip, I'd try it once with ten lakh before moving more.
I don't want to chase forms, a CA in India or a trip, and nothing is charged until the money lands, so the downside is small. The free CA call before anything moves is what gets me past my tax worry.

I have a pile of money sitting in an SBI NRO account I never log into, and I'd happily pay a few hundred dollars not to deal with forms, a CA and time zones. Fee only when the money lands plus a refund guarantee makes it low-risk to try.

I have a lump sum sitting in NRO and I am scared of getting the TDS and 15CA/15CB paperwork wrong, so a CA call before anything moves and a fee taken only on arrival lowers the risk enough to try it. I would still check the FINTRAC number and the bank name myself, and probably send one tranche first.

The free call with a CA and the Form 145/146 filing are exactly what I'm scared of getting wrong with TDS and T1135, and fee-only-on-arrival means little risk for a first small transfer. I'd start with the Essential tier on my own balance and see how it goes.
